User input from request.GET['name'] is used to construct a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and write request.body to it. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../etc/crontab') to write arbitrary files on the filesystem, potentially achieving remote code execution.

XML from request.body is parsed with lxml using XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). This configuration enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, allowing an attacker to read arbitrary files from the server, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service.

User-supplied JSON from request.body is used directly as a MongoDB query filter via find_one(query) without sanitization. An attacker can pass MongoDB query operators (e.g., {'$gt': ''}, {'$where': 'sleep(5000)'}) to extract or manipulate data from the database.
